As the particle size increases, the color changes from red to purple, blue, and finally gold. This is a well-known phenomenon and is true. The color of colloidal solutions indeed depends on the wavelength of light scattered by the dispersed particles. questions.question:
Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be any points on the curves \((x-1)^2+(y+1)^2\) \(=1\) and \(y=x^2\), respectively. The distance between \(P\) and \(Q\) is minimum for some value of the abscissa of \(P\) in the interval

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let the centre of the circle be \(C(1,-1)\), and let \(Q=(t,t^2)\) be a point on the parabola.

We have \(CQ^2=(t-1)^2+(t^2+1)^2=t^4+3t^2-2t+2\).

Also, \(CQ^2-1=t^4+2t^2+(t-1)^2>0\), so every point of the parabola lies outside the circle.

Therefore, the shortest distance from \(Q\) to the circle is \(CQ-1\), and it is minimum when \(CQ\) is minimum.

Let \(H(t)=CQ^2=t^4+3t^2-2t+2\).

Then \(H'(t)=4t^3+6t-2\), and \(H''(t)=12t^2+6>0\).

Therefore, \(H'(t)=0\) has exactly one real root, and that root gives the absolute minimum.

Now \(H'\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)<0\) and \(H'\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)>0\).

Hence the minimizing value satisfies \(\dfrac{1}{4}<t<\dfrac{1}{3}\).

The nearest point \(P\) on the circle lies on the line segment joining \(C\) and \(Q\).

If \(r=CQ\), then \(P=C+\dfrac{Q-C}{r}\).

Therefore, the abscissa of \(P\) is \(x_P=1-\dfrac{1-t}{r}\).

To prove \(x_P>\dfrac{1}{4}\), it is enough to prove \(16(1-t)^2<9r^2\).

Now \(9r^2-16(1-t)^2=9t^4+11t^2+14t+2>0\), so \(x_P>\dfrac{1}{4}\).

To prove \(x_P<\dfrac{1}{2}\), it is enough to prove \(4(1-t)^2>r^2\).

Let \(J(t)=4(1-t)^2-r^2=2-6t+t^2-t^4\).

For \(0<t<\dfrac{1}{3}\), \(J'(t)=-6+2t-4t^3<0\).

Therefore, \(J(t)>J\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)=\dfrac{8}{81}>0\), so \(x_P<\dfrac{1}{2}\).

Hence \(\dfrac{1}{4}<x_P<\dfrac{1}{2}\).

Therefore, the correct option is \(\mathrm{C}\).

\(\vec n_1=\hat i\times(\hat i+\hat j)=\hat k=(0,0,1)\)

The second plane is generated by \(\hat i-\hat j\) and \(\hat i+\hat k\).

Its normal is

\(\vec n_2=(1,-1,0)\times(1,0,1)=(-1,-1,1)\)

A direction vector of their line of intersection is

\(\vec a=\vec n_1\times\vec n_2=(1,-1,0)\)

Given \(\vec b=(1,-2,2)\).

\(\cos\phi=\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}=\dfrac{1+2}{\sqrt2\sqrt9}=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\)

The acute angle is \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

The required obtuse angle is

\(\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\)

The correct option is \(\mathrm{A}\).

questions.question:
Negation of the Boolean expression \( p \Leftrightarrow(q \Rightarrow p) \) is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(X=q\Rightarrow p=(\sim q)\vee p\).

The expression is \(p\leftrightarrow X\).

If \(p=T\), then \(X=T\), so \(p\leftrightarrow X=T\).

If \(p=F\), then \(X=\sim q\).

\(\Rightarrow p\leftrightarrow(q\Rightarrow p)=p\vee q\)

Using De Morgan's law,

\(\Rightarrow \sim(p\leftrightarrow(q\Rightarrow p))=\sim(p\vee q)=(\sim p)\wedge(\sim q)\)

The correct option is \(\mathrm{D}\).

questions.question:
Suppose y=yx be the solution curve to the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}-y=2-e^{-x}\) such that \(\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} y(x)\) is finite. If \(a\) and \(b\) are respectively the \(x-\) and \(y-\) intercepts of the tangent to the curve at \(x=0\), then the value of \(a-4 b\) is equal to .............

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=2-e^{-x}\)

The integrating factor is \(e^{-x}\).

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{-x}y)=2e^{-x}-e^{-2x}\)

\(\Rightarrow e^{-x}y=-2e^{-x}+\dfrac{1}{2}e^{-2x}+C\)

\(\Rightarrow y=-2+\dfrac{1}{2}e^{-x}+Ce^x\)

\(\because \displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}y(x)\) is finite,

\(C=0\)

\(\Rightarrow y=-2+\dfrac{1}{2}e^{-x}\)

At \(x=0\), \(y=-\dfrac{3}{2}\)

Also, \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{1}{2}e^{-x}\)

\(\Rightarrow \left.\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=0}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\)

The tangent at \(x=0\) is \(y+\dfrac{3}{2}=-\dfrac{x}{2}\)

\(\Rightarrow x+2y+3=0\)

Its \(x\)-intercept is \(a=-3\), and its \(y\)-intercept is \(b=-\dfrac{3}{2}\).

\(a-4b=-3-4\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow a-4b=3\)

Option B is correct.

questions.question:
If the sum of solutions of the system of equations \(2 \sin ^2 \theta\) \(-\cos 2 \theta=0\) and \(2 \cos ^2 \theta+3 \sin \theta=0\) in the interval \([0,2 \pi]\) is \(k \pi\), then \(k\) is equal to ____

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
\(2 \sin ^2 \theta=\cos 2 \theta=1-2 \sin ^2 \theta\)
\( \Rightarrow 4 \sin ^2 \theta=1 \Rightarrow \sin \theta= \pm \frac{1}{2}\)

\(\Rightarrow  \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5 \pi}{6}, \frac{7 \pi}{6}, \frac{11 \pi}{6}\)
Now, \(2 \cos ^2\theta+3 \sin \theta=0\)
\(2 \sin ^2 \theta-3 \sin \theta-2=0\)
\(2 \sin ^2 \theta-4 \sin \theta+\sin \theta-2=0\)
\((2 \sin \theta+1)(\sin \theta-2)=0\)
\(\Rightarrow \sin \theta=-\frac{1}{2}, \theta=\frac{7 \pi}{6}, \frac{11 \pi}{6}\)
Sum \(=\frac{7 \pi}{6}+\frac{11 \pi}{6}=3 \pi \Rightarrow k=3\)

questions.question:
The largest value of a, for which the perpendicuar distance of the plane containing the lines \( r=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})+\lambda(\hat{i}+a \hat{j}-\hat{k}) \) and \( r=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})+\mu(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}-a \hat{k}) \) from the point \( (2,1,4) \) is \( \sqrt{3} \), is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The two lines pass through \(A=(1,1,0)\).

Their direction vectors are

\(\vec d_1=(1,a,-1),\quad \vec d_2=(-1,1,-a)\)

A normal of their plane is

\(\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=(1-a^2,a+1,a+1)\)

For \(a\ne -1\), this normal is proportional to \((1-a,1,1)\).

The plane through \(A\) is

\((1-a)(x-1)+(y-1)+z=0\)

For \(P=(2,1,4)\), its perpendicular distance from the plane is

\(\dfrac{|(1-a)(2-1)+(1-1)+4|}{\sqrt{(1-a)^2+1+1}}=\dfrac{|5-a|}{\sqrt{(1-a)^2+2}}\)

Given this distance is \(\sqrt3\).

\(\dfrac{(5-a)^2}{(1-a)^2+2}=3\)

\(\Rightarrow (5-a)^2=3\left((1-a)^2+2\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow a^2-10a+25=3a^2-6a+9\)

\(\Rightarrow 2a^2+4a-16=0\)

\(\Rightarrow a^2+2a-8=0\)

\(\Rightarrow (a+4)(a-2)=0\)

\(\Rightarrow a=-4,2\)

The largest value is \(2\).

questions.question:
The plane passing through the line \(L: \ell x-y+3(1-\ell) z=1\), \(x+2 y-z=2\) and perpendicular to the plane \(3 x+2 y+z=6\) is \(3 x-8 y+7 z=4\). If \(\theta\) is the acute angle between the line \(L\) and the \(y\) axis, then \(415 \cos ^2 \theta\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(F_1=\ell x-y+3(1-\ell)z-1\)

\(F_2=x+2y-z-2\)

The plane \(3x-8y+7z-4=0\) contains the line \(L\), so

\(pF_1+qF_2=3x-8y+7z-4\)

Comparing the coefficient of \(y\) and the constant term,

\(-p+2q=-8\)

\(-p-2q=-4\)

\(\Rightarrow p=6,\quad q=-1\)

Comparing the coefficient of \(x\),

\(6\ell-1=3\)

\(\Rightarrow \ell=\dfrac23\)

The line \(L\) is the intersection of the planes with normals

\(\vec n_1=\left(\dfrac23,-1,1\right)\) and \(\vec n_2=(1,2,-1)\).

Using the proportional normal \((2,-3,3)\),

\(\vec d=(2,-3,3)\times(1,2,-1)=(-3,5,7)\)

Let \(\theta\) be the acute angle between \(L\) and the \(y\)-axis.

\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{|5|}{\sqrt{(-3)^2+5^2+7^2}}=\dfrac5{\sqrt{83}}\)

\(\Rightarrow 415\cos^2\theta=415\left(\dfrac{25}{83}\right)=125\)

The required answer is \(125\).

questions.question:
The mean and standard deviation of 40 observations are 30 and 5 respectively. It was noticed that two of these observations 12 and 10 were wrongly recorded. If \( \sigma \) is the standard deviation of the data after omitting the two wrong observations from the data, then \( 38 \sigma^{2} \) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For the original \(40\) observations, \(\sum x_i=40\times 30=1200\).

Using \(\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n}-\bar{x}^{\,2}\), we get \(\sum x_i^2=40(5^2+30^2)=37000\).

After omitting \(12\) and \(10\), the number of observations is \(38\).

\(\Rightarrow \text{New sum}=1200-12-10=1178\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{New mean}=\dfrac{1178}{38}=31\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{New sum of squares}=37000-12^2-10^2=36756\)

\(\Rightarrow \sigma^2=\dfrac{36756}{38}-31^2=\dfrac{119}{19}\)

\(\Rightarrow 38\sigma^2=38\times\dfrac{119}{19}=238\)

The required value is \(238\).
